method.title: How we work
method.intro: Nukkad is a small team and some software. Here's exactly what each does, what we count, and where we can be wrong.
method.s1: We split the area into hexagons about 0.1 km² each, roughly a block. For each kind of shop, a block's catchment is the walk most people will make for it: about 10 minutes for a pharmacy, 5 for tea.
method.s2: Shops from OpenStreetMap, and Google Maps where we've checked it. People from WorldPop's population estimates. Then our field team walks the streets and counts what maps miss, including carts and home shops.
method.s3: We compare people to shops. If a block has 1 pharmacy for every 7,100 people within walking distance and the area has 1 for every 3,900, that block scores higher. Busy streets, what neighbours tell us, complaints in reviews, and high rents each nudge the score a little. Software does this arithmetic the same way every time; nobody can change a number by hand except an analyst, within 15 points, with a written reason.
method.s4: We say how sure we are based on how much we've checked, not on how high the score is. Map data alone is an early signal. A count on foot or enough neighbours' answers makes us fairly sure. Both, recently, make us confident.
method.s5: Software drafts the plain-language explanation from the numbers. A check rejects any sentence with a number that isn't in the evidence. Then an analyst reads it, edits it, and signs it. Blocks nobody has checked are marked "Not reviewed yet".
method.s6: We scored the area as the map looked two years ago and checked where new shops opened and survived. We publish those results, good or bad, and only show kinds of shop where we beat simple guesses.
method.s7: Informal sellers, rent negotiations, how good a shop owner is, and family or community ties that bring customers. Maps of Guwahati are uneven: busy streets are mapped better than quiet lanes. A high score is a reason to look closer, not a promise.
method.s8: If you answer our survey we keep your email (to stop duplicate answers) and the block you live in, never your address. We show neighbours' answers only once 20 or more people nearby have answered. You can delete everything from your account page.

source_rows.survey: Short surveys from verified residents, shown only in groups of 20 or more.
source_rows.rent: Asking rents noted by our team from owners and brokers. Never scraped.

survey.start_intro: 8 to 12 quick questions about where you go today. About 2 minutes. Your answers help people decide what to open on your street.
survey.consent_body: We keep your email to stop duplicate answers, and the block you live in (about 0.1 km²), never your address. We use your answers only to understand what this area needs. We show neighbours' answers only once 20 or more people nearby have answered. You can delete your answers any time from your account page.
